title: Full Marathon Races in Indonesia: 2026 Calendar
intro: Seven full marathons run across Indonesia between August and November 2026, and August alone carries three of them, so runners chasing a fall marathon here have decisions to make early in the season. The set ranges from Bekasi and Depok on Java's dense urban fringe to the volcanic highlands of Tosari for the Bromo Marathon and the temple approach of the Bank Jateng Borobudur Marathon in Magelang. Bali's Gianyar hosts the Maybank Marathon in August, while Jakarta stretches its running festival across four days in October. Every race pairs the 42.195km distance with shorter options, from half marathons down to 2.5km fun runs, so the choice often comes down to setting and month rather than distance alone.

faqs.question: Which month has the most full marathon options in Indonesia?
faqs.answer: August 2026 is the busiest, with three races: Bekasi Marathon, BTN UI Green Marathon in Depok, and Maybank Marathon in Gianyar, Bali. September, October, and November each hold one or two events, so August is where most of the scheduling overlap and decision-making happens.

faqs.question: What makes the Bromo Marathon different from the other Indonesian marathons on this list?
faqs.answer: The Bromo Marathon takes place in Tosari, East Java, in a highland volcanic setting rather than the urban courses found in Bekasi, Depok, or Jakarta. It runs in September and offers the widest distance spread of the group, from a 2.5km option up through the full 42.195km.

faqs.question: Is the Jakarta Running Festival a single-day race?
faqs.answer: No. The Jakarta Running Festival 2026 spans four days, from October 22 to October 25, unlike the other events on this list which are single-day races. It offers the same distance range of 42.195/21.1/10/5km as several others.

editorial_pick: The Maybank Marathon (84/100) in Gianyar, Bali is the standout here -- Indonesia's only World Athletics Elite Label road race and a Boston Marathon qualifier since 2013, run through rice paddies and Balinese villages at a 4:30am start.
